rows.summary: This guide demonstrates how to access the Kubernetes API from within a pod, including using official client libraries, directly accessing the REST API, and using kubectl proxy.

This document explains how to configure service accounts for pods in Kubernetes, including using the default service account, opting out of API credential automounting, and manually creating API tokens.
This document explains how to extend the existing Service IP range assigned to a Kubernetes cluster, including adding a new ServiceCIDR, deleting a ServiceCIDR, and Kubernetes Service CIDR policies.

This document outlines the process of migrating from PodSecurityPolicy to the built-in PodSecurity Admission Controller in Kubernetes. It provides a step-by-step guide for deciding if Pod Security Admission is suitable, reviewing namespace permissions, simplifying and standardizing PodSecurityPolicies, updating namespaces, reviewing namespace creation processes, and disabling PodSecurityPolicy.
This document provides guidelines for designing and implementing admission webhooks in Kubernetes to avoid common failure scenarios and ensure compatibility with Kubernetes API changes.

Dynamic volume provisioning allows storage volumes to be created on-demand, eliminating the need for cluster administrators to pre-provision storage. Users can request dynamically provisioned storage by including a storage class in their PersistentVolumeClaim.

This document provides an overview of different approaches to manage Kubernetes objects using the `kubectl` command-line tool. It covers imperative commands, imperative object configuration, and declarative object configuration, along with their trade-offs and examples.
This document provides guidelines for improving the security posture of the Kubernetes scheduler, including configuration options for authentication, authorization, networking, and TLS.

This document provides an overview of how Kubernetes implements and controls API access, including authentication, admission controllers, authorization, certificate signing requests, service accounts, and kubelet authentication and authorization.
CustomResourceDefinition is an API object that defines a new custom API to extend the Kubernetes API server, allowing for custom resources when built-in API resources are insufficient.
This document outlines the minimum Linux kernel version requirements for various Kubernetes features and components.

This document explains the concept of a probe in Kubernetes, which is a check performed by the kubelet against a running container to define its state and health, and inform the container's lifecycle.

This document explains how to define and use declarative admission policies in Kubernetes, including validating and mutating admission policies, policy elements, and how to test and use these policies.
This tutorial shows how to run a sample NGINX application on Kubernetes using minikube, including setting up a cluster, checking status, opening the dashboard, and creating a deployment and service.
